items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: At that particular time, I think I was rooming with Taswell Baird, little Joe we called him, the trombone player.

ctx.x: And we left there, and we caught the train and went down to this little border town across from Juarez, Mexico -- El Paso, Texas. That's where, during those days, you would change trains to go to Los Angeles or points West. So we get to El Paso, you change trains, and we have a wait for the next train of about three hours. So everybody, in a situation like that, you always put your bags in a locker or something and go around, and see what's happening in the town or whatever, and just find a way to kill three…

At that particular time, I think I was rooming with Taswell Baird, little Joe we called him, the trombone player. And so he and I, when all this stuff was happening in Texas and these guys were buying all this stuff, he tells me... He said, "Don't bother. We'll get us a small bag, and when we get to El Paso, I know a Mexican over in Juarez and he'll give me (I forgot how much he said) for little or nothing." So he and I were roommates, we're brothers, so I say, "Okay, whatever you say." It was my first time out…
